requirement: The frontend backend opens a session and retains its handle across calls; the Rust session owns configuration runtime workers SQLite connections per-account DuckDB connections authentication and IMAP connections.
rationale: Provides a stateful backend with explicit resource ownership

requirement: Validate configuration and transformer registry acquire exclusive portable root writer ownership open and migrate SQLite then lazily open per-account DuckDB; roll back partial initialization and return no handle on failure.
rationale: Prevents partial initialization and concurrent independent writers

requirement: Atomically reject new calls cancel and drain workers fence unfinished durable claims close IMAP and database connections clear secrets release process ownership and invalidate the handle; close waits for bounded network timeouts and cleanup.
rationale: No workers may access freed session resources

requirement: Allow calls from multiple host threads through a synchronized handle registry; serialize configuration authentication mutation SQLite writes and per-account DuckDB writes while bounded workers run independent tasks.
rationale: Rust values and connections do not cross the C boundary

requirement: Calls already admitted retain session ownership; close marks closing and waits for admitted calls and workers before disposal. Unknown closed or stale handles return session.invalid; a second close returns session.invalid.
rationale: Defines deterministic use after close and concurrent close behavior

requirement: auth.set accepts accountID and a mechanisms object with exactly one of PLAIN XOAUTH2 OAUTHBEARER SCRAM-SHA-256; require nonempty username and the corresponding password or accessToken and reject unknown fields nulls and multiple mechanisms.
rationale: The supplied four-mechanism catalogue describes alternatives rather than simultaneous credentials

requirement: Require verified TLS before sending credentials and verify server capability for the selected mechanism; never silently downgrade. SCRAM-SHA-256 must validate the server signature using a standards-compliant adapter.
rationale: Mechanism selection has explicit failure semantics

requirement: Keep credentials only in owned session memory per account; auth.set replaces them increments an in-memory auth generation and closes old IMAP connections. Late work using an old generation cannot restore authentication state or commit stale results.
rationale: Supports explicit token or password replacement across concurrent work

requirement: The host owns OAuth consent token acquisition refresh and secret persistence; expired or missing credentials produce authentication-required and network work blocks without consuming processing attempts until auth.set and explicit resume.
rationale: No OS credential store or provider setup service is required

requirement: auth.clear cancels and drains account network work clears credentials closes authenticated connections and leaves durable metadata intact. Close restart and process termination always require fresh credentials.
rationale: Logout and recovery separate durable work from ephemeral authentication

requirement: Do not persist secrets in SQLite DuckDB Parquet configuration task payloads logs tracing events exports or error details; avoid logging authentication request bytes and IMAP SASL exchanges and clear owned secret buffers on replacement and close where practical.
rationale: Host-owned input buffers remain the host responsibility

requirement: Expose ABI version 1 fixed-width status values an opaque process-local session token and pointer-length byte buffers; version JSON payloads independently and reject unsupported versions and unknown methods.
rationale: Separates stable C layout from evolving payload schemas

requirement: All JSON uses validated UTF-8 length-delimited buffers; copy borrowed input before returning and free Rust-owned output exactly once with selenetide_buffer_free. Never expose Rust String Vec trait objects or references through C.

Return structured sanitized errors with stable codes and retryability; initialize outputs on every valid-pointer path and contain panics at every extern boundary. Allocation failure may return an empty buffer and status; a compromised session rejects further work until close.
rationale: Errors cannot unwind into foreign code

requirement: Long sync fetch processing query and export calls return operation IDs immediately; status result and cancel methods operate within the owning session. Cancellation is cooperative; durable domain run IDs remain resumable after reopen while session operation IDs expire.
rationale: Keeps foreign calls independent of a host async runtime

requirement: events.poll is nonblocking and returns bounded ordered events and a next cursor; queue overflow or an old cursor returns events.gap with a snapshot refresh requirement; events and result pages obey configured byte limits.
rationale: Bounds memory and makes lost progress explicit

requirement: Map subsystem Promise operations to JSON requests and operation IDs and AsyncIterable events to polling; the TypeScript files are host-adapter sketches rather than native C signatures. Transformer registration remains Rust-internal in v1.
rationale: Avoids requiring frontend callbacks or generic types in the C ABI

requirement: UniFFI is optional for generated target-language records enums objects and async conveniences over the same Rust session model; its generated scaffolding is distinct from the public C ABI and must be version-pinned with its bindings.
rationale: A frontend may choose direct C integration without UniFFI

requirement: Field tables describe logical entities. Map IDs to canonical UUID TEXT booleans to checked INTEGER 0 or 1 dates to INTEGER UTC Unix milliseconds JSON to TEXT and bytes to BLOB; collections use foreign keys or join tables with declared uniqueness and delete rules.
rationale: Replaces managed object storage with explicit relational mappings
